title: gpu-age-profile-depreciation-reorder-triggers
content:
Purpose:
Short working spreadsheet to combine age-profile, simple depreciation proxies, utilization burn-rates and a deterministic reorder-point heuristic for regional ordering windows. Intention is to surface near-term procurement needs and to bake a repeatable trigger that can feed the procurement pipeline (monthly order cycles + emergency spot lanes).

Notes / assumptions:
- SKUs tracked: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, L40-80GB, A10-24GB, T4-16GB.
- Depreciation proxy = operational-risk weight (not accounting depreciation for accounting) — higher age buckets incur higher failure/repair and performance variability risk.
- Utilization measured as 7-day rolling active-GPU-hours / available-GPU-hours.
- Burn-rate = average GPU-hours consumed per day for a region and SKU.
- Lead times (procurement + transit + rack-ops) are region+SKU specific and updated monthly from vendors.
- Safety buffer = max(10% of available inventory, 3 * per-region daily burn-rate) or a minimum of 2 GPUs for small fleets.

Summary table (flattened view used in sheet columns):
Columns: SKU | Region | Total Inventory | Age 0-6mo % | Age 6-18mo % | Age 18-36mo % | Age 36mo+ % | Avg utilization % | Daily burn-rate (GPU-hrs/day) | Estimated MTBF-risk (qualitative) | Lead time (days) | Days of runway (inventory / daily equivalent) | Reorder point (GPUs) | Procurement priority | Notes

Rows (examples, values are illustrative):
A100-80GB | us-west1 | 240 | 42% | 38% | 15% | 5% | 72% | 1,440 | medium | 65 | 33 | 36 | high | Consider split order: 60% A100 reserve + 40% H100 trial
H100-80GB | us-east4 | 96 | 28% | 44% | 20% | 8% | 81% | 768 | high | 78 | 25 | 18 | urgent | High-util, prioritize dedicated-capacity purchases and available reserved capacity swap
L40-80GB | eu-west1 | 120 | 50% | 30% | 15% | 5% | 62% | 540 | low | 40 | 48 | 22 | medium | Good candidate for spot/lease expansion if short lead time
A10-24GB | ap-southeast1 | 48 | 60% | 30% | 8% | 2% | 34% | 120 | low | 32 | 40 | 6 | low | Lower priority, keep 2-unit safety min in region
T4-16GB | us-east4 | 64 | 10% | 30% | 40% | 20% | 18% | 64 | high (age) | 28 | 28 | 8 | medium | Many older units; consider phased refresh during next 6mo orders

Trigger logic (deterministic heuristic implemented in sheet formulas):
1) Compute daily-equivalent GPUs = daily burn-rate / 24 (GPU-hours -> GPU-days), round up to 0.5 increments.
2) Days_of_runway = Total Inventory / daily-equivalent GPUs.
3) Effective lead = Lead_time_days + vendor_queue_slack (vendor queue slack = 0 for currently contracted reserved purchases, or an added 14 days for uncontracted RFPs).
4) Safety_buffer_units = max(ceil(0.10 * Total Inventory), ceil(3 * daily-equivalent GPUs), 2).
5) Reorder_point = ceil(daily-equivalent GPUs * Effective_lead) + Safety_buffer_units + expected_retirements_in_period (retirements = count of GPUs in age 36mo+ * 0.02 per month assumed).
6) Priority assignment: if Days_of_runway < Effective_lead + 14 => urgent; if Days_of_runway < Effective_lead * 1.5 => high; if Days_of_runway < Effective_lead * 2.5 => medium; else low.

Procurement pipeline notes: 
- Monthly cadence: Orders finalized by day 10 of each month for delivery windows in the following 6-10 weeks for long-lead SKUs (A100/H100).
- Emergency window: we maintain 10% cross-region buffer that can be hot-moved (region-to-region transfer) with a 7–14 day transit SLA — only for less regulated workloads.
- Lease/spot lane: for shortfalls under 30 days runway, prefer short-term rentals (colocated partners) for L40/A10/T4 where performance tradeoffs acceptable.
- Budget gating: any single order > $1.2M requires headcount approval; multiple small orders can be batched by SKU to hit volume discounts.

Refresh & retirement policy (operational recommendation):
- Plan a 24–36 month rolling refresh for high-util SKUs (A100/H100); accelerate if average utilization >80% and age 18-36mo >30%.
- For low-util SKUs used for embeddings and small workloads (T4/A10), prefer mixing leased capacity and phased refresh.
- Track EOL notifications from vendors (NVIDIA) and shift ordering timeline + reserve an additional 12 weeks when EOL announced.

Quick action checklist (for on-call infra + procurement ops):
- If any region SKU enters "urgent" priority: alert procurement channel, open emergency RFP, evaluate short-term lease, flag potential traffic reroute.
- If aggregated fleet-level runway drops below 45 days: prepare conversation with finance for bridging-capex and pre-approve one small emergency order equivalent to 5% fleet.
- If a single rack failure impacts >5% of a region's GPU inventory, move 10% cross-region buffer and trigger SRE playbook.

Open questions / next steps (notes-to-self):
- Need better vendor lead-time telemetry: ask procurement to log estimated ship dates vs actual delivery to compute bias adjustments by SKU and region.
- Model sensitivity to utilization spikes: run Monte Carlo stress (not in this sheet) for 30/60/90 day surge scenarios.
- Validate MTBF proxy against historical failure incidents from SRE incident DB (INFRA-ops).
- Add a column for contract status (reserved/spot/leased) to better route reorder actions.

Revision history:
- 2024-01-10 initial draft and age-bucket breakdown
- 2024-02-12 added reorder-point heuristic and procurement priority rules
- 2024-02-28 updated lead times for H100 in us-east4 and added emergency checklist
